scenes.headline: How a depth prior keeps a small window on scale
scenes.sub: MetricTrail: DPVO, metric depth, and DINOv3 features
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Odo! Today, how NVIDIA's MetricTrail tracks a camera through a very long video without a long memory.

scenes.text: Tie every patch's depth to a single-image metric depth prediction, and a small optimisation window stops losing track of what a metre is.
scenes.mark: stops losing track of what a metre is
scenes.say: Tie every patch's depth to a single image depth prediction in metres. Then a small window can no longer forget what a metre is.

steps.say: Each frame goes through MoGe-2, which predicts depth in metres from that one image.
That depth seeds every new patch, and stays inside bundle adjustment as a soft constraint.
Frozen DINOv3 features reach the patch matcher through small learned adapters.
The matcher predicts where each patch lands, and a ten pose window solves for camera and depth.

scenes.title: The factor that holds scale
scenes.text: E = E_DPVO + λ Σ Huber(log ρ - log ρ̂)

parts.say: The usual reprojection error cannot see scale. Stretch everything and it does not change.
This term compares each patch's depth with the predicted depth, as a ratio.
Huber caps the pull past a ratio of about one point three five, so a wrong prediction cannot drag the geometry.

left.title: DPVO
items: Median depth of the last three frames
left.say: DPVO seeds a new patch with the median depth of recent patches, which copies forward any drift.

right.title: MetricTrail
items: Its own predicted depth in metres
Kept as a factor after frame 12
right.say: MetricTrail seeds it with its own predicted depth, and keeps that prediction as a factor.

steps.say: Here is plain DPVO on KITTI zero zero. The green estimate wanders far off the grey ground truth.
Add the metric prior, with no retraining, and the path snaps onto the loop.

scenes.title: KITTI average trajectory error
scenes.say: Across KITTI, the depth prior is worth more than everything else combined.

scenes.text: Long-video drift was mostly one missing term: an absolute reference for scale at every patch.
scenes.say: For this estimator, long video drift was mostly one missing term. An absolute reference for scale, at every patch.
Metric depth seeds each patch. A Huber factor keeps the scale. And DINOv3 sharpens the matches.
